question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund is a close-ended Category III AIF with a 5-year tenure expiring December 31, 2029. The Manager wishes to extend the tenure. What is permitted under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Unlimited extensions of 1-year each, each requiring simple majority of investors by value
Up to 2 additional years (in two 1-year extensions), each with approval of two-thirds of investors by value of investment
A single 5-year extension with Trustee board approval only
No extension is permitted; the fund must wind up on tenure expiry

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Close-ended Cat III AIFs can be extended by up to 2 additional years via two separate 1-year extensions, each requiring approval of two-thirds of investors BY VALUE of their investment. Absent consent or after extended tenure, the fund must wind up. **The Trap:** Option A removes the cap. Option C invents a Trustee-only path. Option D denies any extension. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D tests the same formula for Cat I/II close-ended. XIX-E frames it against a Cat III long-short scheme. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Start investor outreach ~6 months before tenure expiry. Use Form for majority-by-value voting. LVFs (Cat III) have even longer extension rights (up to 5 years) subject to contribution-agreement terms.
